summary: Each row of Pascal's triangle comes from the row above: a 1, then the sums of neighbouring pairs, then a 1. We keep only the current row and rebuild it N times (T13 — building a table from smaller answers).

blocks.title: Read N
blocks.text: Copy the prompt exactly, including the parentheses: `Enter the number of rows (N): `.

blocks.title: Print the header
blocks.text: The header comes before the rows and includes N: `Pascal's Triangle with 5 rows:`. The f-string's double quotes let the apostrophe sit inside safely.

blocks.title: Print N rows
blocks.text: `print(*row)` prints the numbers separated by spaces, with no brackets or commas.

blocks.title: Build the next row
blocks.text: `row[i] + row[i + 1]` adds each pair of neighbours; `range(len(row) - 1)` stops before `i + 1` runs off the end. Wrapping with `[1] + … + [1]` adds the edges. From `[1]` the middle part is empty, giving `[1, 1]`.

complexity: Time O(N²) with N ≤ 30 → under 500 additions.
pitfalls: Building the next row in place while still reading the old one.
